task.description: WF-02 Step 1 — design lib/letflow/design/req074-identity-group-routes.md covering route wiring for the seven group-management handlers (handleCreateGroup, handleAddGroupMember, handleListGroups, handleDeleteGroup, handleListGroupMembersArray, handleListGroupMembers, handleRemoveGroupMember) into lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex as an extension of REQ-073's existing five user-CRUD routes, reusing its with_authorized_scope/4 preamble and user_map/1 unchanged. Load-bearing investigation: read R-Co's actual route table (src/main.zig, not just identity.zig) to determine whether handleListGroupMembers and handleListGroupMembersArray are both served, and whether handleRemoveGroupMember is actually routed, then design accordingly rather than assuming from the handler file alone.
acceptance_criteria: Every acceptance criterion maps to a concrete design element
All new types/schemas are defined with field-level detail (including the new group_members join table, not present in this codebase today)
DB schema changes fully described (table, columns, indexes, constraints) -- group_members migration, plus groups table additions (display_name, description, unique index on name)
Open questions listed explicitly, not silently resolved
No implementation code (.ex/.exs bodies) present -- signatures and type shapes only

result.summary: Wrote lib/letflow/design/req074-identity-group-routes.md. LOAD-BEARING FINDING (AC6): read R-Co's real route table at src/main.zig:1377-1442 (not just identity.zig's handler file) -- grep -n "handleListGroupMembers(\|handleRemoveGroupMember" src/main.zig returns ZERO registration hits for either symbol. main.zig only wires handleListGroupMembersArray (bare array, fixed page_size 200) at GET /groups/:id/members; handleListGroupMembers (the cursor-paginated, PLATFORM_ADMIN-gated variant) is real, tested code (identity.zig's own TC-IDN-02-03) that is never reachable through any route R-Co serves -- dead from the route table's perspective. Design decision: port ONE endpoint at GET /groups/:id/members, using cursor pagination (matching AC4's own explicit requirement and REQ-067), not the served bare-array shape -- same kind of deliberate, stated divergence REQ-073 made for list_users/2's cursor-vs-offset choice. SECOND FINDING (not explicitly asked for, surfaced anyway): handleRemoveGroupMember is ALSO never routed -- R-Co's live DELETE /groups/:id/members (no user_id segment) is inline bulk-remove-all-members logic in main.zig, not handleRemoveGroupMember at all. Design ports handleRemoveGroupMember's single-member semantics at DELETE /groups/:id/members/:user_id anyway (matching the requirement's explicit handler list and REST shape), explicitly NOT replicating the bulk-remove-all behavior R-Co's live route actually serves -- flagged as OQ-1 for REVIEWER since no acceptance criterion asks for bulk removal and this is a larger divergence-from-actually-served-behavior than the first finding. AC5 finding: read identity/service.zig's deleteGroup (calls registry.deleteGroupIfEmpty) and registry.zig:1178-1217's SQL directly -- R-Co REFUSES to delete a non-empty group (DELETE ... WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM group_members ...)), and the refusal is mapped to the IDENTICAL 404 group_not_found response a genuinely nonexistent group id gets -- no separate 409. Ported as Identity.delete_group/2 returning :ok | {:error, :not_found_or_has_members}, one unified atom. Six new Letflow.Identity functions named (create_group/2, add_group_member/3, list_groups/1, delete_group/2, list_group_members/3, remove_group_member/3). Domain-schema gaps found and designed: no group_members table exists anywhere in this codebase today (new tenant-scoped migration + Letflow.Identity.GroupMember schema needed); groups table is missing display_name/description columns and a unique index on name (needed for duplicate_group_name mapping) -- additive migration designed. endpoint_policy_key(method, "/groups" <> _rest) already covers all six new routes with zero authorization-module changes needed (unlike REQ-073's one added clause). Cross-tenant-membership test (AC2/INV-1/INV-5) designed to assert both byte-identical 404 AND a direct Repo.aggregate(GroupMember, :count, prefix: tenant_a.schema_name) == 0 after the attempt. Tenant-isolation (AC3), pagination (AC4, new "G:" cursor prefix reusing R-Co's own literal from identity_service.zig:1107), and delete-with-members (AC5) test designs all included with full ExUnit specs.

issues.description: OQ-1 (largest, flagged for REVIEWER specifically): this design ports handleRemoveGroupMember's single-member DELETE semantics at /groups/:id/members/:user_id, a route R-Co's own table never binds to that handler -- R-Co's live bodyless DELETE /groups/:id/members instead bulk-removes every member. No acceptance criterion asks for bulk removal, so it is not added, but this divergence from R-Co's actually-served behavior is larger than the AC6 finding and deserves explicit sign-off rather than being treated as equivalent in kind.

OQ-2 through OQ-9 in the design doc: dual user_id/user_ids[0] body-parsing fallback worth preserving (OQ-2); not porting handleListGroupMembers's R-Co-only PLATFORM_ADMIN-exclusive gate in favor of the shared :GroupsManage policy -- a real behavioral narrowing-removal, flagged for REVIEWER (OQ-3); cursor tiebreak field for list_group_members/3 (OQ-4); list_groups/1 sort order not confirmed against registry.zig's listGroups SQL, out of this requirement's named source-file scope (OQ-5); raw-SQL vs Ecto.Query not-exists/1 for delete_group/2's guarded delete, not security-relevant either way (OQ-6); whether group_members needs a surrogate :id PK (OQ-7); whether member_count is computed into group_map/1's response given R-Co's shipped shape includes it but no AC requires it (OQ-8); whether add-member's response includes added_at (OQ-9). None block implementation.
